If you are using corrugated pipe it will help a lot. The corrugations cause turbulence in the water as it flows through the pipe. The turbulence keeps the silt from building up.

Normal practice is embed the pipe within a layer of stone with the stone being surrounded (wrapped in) a layer of filter fabric. The filter fabric, in theory, allows water to pass in and out while limiting the amount of dirt that can get into and clog the stone.

The big box stores sell fabric covered pipe but I have found this to be well beyond my budget. The least expensive options that I have found is to buy the pipe and the filter fabric separately ( at the big box store) and have the stone delivered from the closest quarry or garden supply outlet, etc. This is much less expensive and less strenuous then buying it, by the bag, from the big box store. Also, I find that no matter how careful that I am I usually underestimate the quantity of stone that I need. Since I always manage to find a use for it, I usually try to round up my quantities when buying bulk loads - just keep an eye on future projects that might be able to absorb any surplus - it's no fun to trip over a pile of stone, mulch etc. sitting in your driveway for any period of time.
